advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the autolander a distinct host port (e.g. AUTOLANDER_PORT=8090) so it does not collide with Gerrit's fixed 127.0.0.1:8080 host binding.
evidence: Gerrit binds host 8080: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:38 `- "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"` with comment `8080: Gerrit HTTP — published to host loopback`
Autolander binds the SAME host port: diff docker-compose `- "127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080"`
fetch-secrets.sh:114 `echo "AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080"` (so the default is actually used, not overridden)
nginx catch-all proxies Gerrit on the same port: infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:86 `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;`
advisory.finding: The autolander compose service publishes 127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080 and fetch-secrets.sh writes AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080, which collides with the Gerrit container's fixed 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 host binding — `docker compose up` cannot bind two containers to the same host loopback endpoint, so the autolander deploy fails, and nginx's catch-all `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080` (Gerrit) contends with the /autolander/status route target.
scenarios: Any deploy that brings up both Gerrit and autolander on the host — the second bind to 127.0.0.1:8080 fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Set AUTOLANDER_PORT to a free host port (e.g. 8090) in fetch-secrets.sh and update the ${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080} default + AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL and nginx AUTOLANDER_PORT accordingly; the container port can stay 8080.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Point AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL at the autolander's real (non-colliding) host port once the port collision is resolved.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:51 `AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL="${AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL:-http://localhost:8080/}"  # auto-lander status endpoint (NOT Gerrit)`
Gerrit is the actual occupant of host 8080 (docker-compose.yml:38)
advisory.finding: The autodeploy autolander health check targets http://localhost:8080/, the same host port Gerrit is published on, despite the inline comment saying '(NOT Gerrit)'. Because of the port collision it either hits Gerrit or fails; either way it does not reliably probe the autolander status endpoint.
scenarios: Autolander deploy health probe after `docker compose up`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the commit messages and smoke-check header with the actual project.config change (only `rebase` was granted; rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader is not a ref permission).
evidence: setup-project.sh commit message: '... + rebase/rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant (auto-lander FFO rebase, S5b) ...'
project.config comment contradicts it: infra/gerrit/project.config:68-69 'there is no separate `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` ref permission; that form is silently ignored'

smoke-check header claims both were added: infra/gerrit/smoke-check-autolander.sh:8-10 'hold BOTH the per-ref `rebase` AND `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` access rights — the grant added to infra/gerrit/project.config'
advisory.finding: The commit message and setup-project.sh's commit message advertise a `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` grant, but project.config only adds `rebase` and its own comment states `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` is not a real ref permission and is 'silently ignored'. The smoke-check header also asserts the bot must hold 'BOTH the per-ref rebase AND rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader access rights — the grant added to project.config', which contradicts what was actually added. These artifacts describe a grant that does not exist.
scenarios: A future maintainer trusts the commit/smoke-check text and looks for a rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader ref grant that was intentionally not added.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Change the autolander host port default away from Gerrit's 8080 (e.g. AUTOLANDER_PORT=8081) so 127.0.0.1 bindings do not collide.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:38: - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080" (gerrit)
docker-compose.yml:130: - "127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080" (autolander)
fetch-secrets.sh:114: echo "AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080"
Dockerfile.autolander: ENV AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080 / EXPOSE 8080
advisory.finding: Host-port collision: the autolander service publishes 127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080 and fetch-secrets.sh writes AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080, but the gerrit service already binds 127.0.0.1:8080:8080. Two containers cannot bind the same host loopback port, so `docker compose up` fails with a port-allocation error under the default configuration.
scenarios: compose-up.sh runs fetch-secrets.sh (writes AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080) then `docker compose up -d`, which fails because 127.0.0.1:8080 is already bound by gerrit
advisory.suggested_fix: Set AUTOLANDER_PORT to a non-8080 value in fetch-secrets.sh and the compose default (and update the nginx/autodeploy references), since Gerrit owns 127.0.0.1:8080.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL from the actual autolander host port (not hardcoded 8080, which is Gerrit's) so the post-deploy probe targets the autolander status endpoint.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:51: AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL="${AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL:-http://localhost:8080/}"  # auto-lander status endpoint (NOT Gerrit)
docker-compose.yml:38: gerrit binds 127.0.0.1:8080:8080
fetch-secrets.sh single-sources AUTOLANDER_PORT but this URL does not consume it
advisory.finding: autodeploy.sh's AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL defaults to http://localhost:8080/, which is Gerrit's published port, so the post-deploy 'auto-lander status endpoint' health probe (and rollback trigger) actually probes Gerrit rather than the autolander; it is also hardcoded instead of derived from AUTOLANDER_PORT, so it drifts if the port is changed to resolve the collision.
scenarios: An autolander deploy where the loop is actually broken still sees a 200 from Gerrit on :8080 and is declared healthy, skipping the intended rollback
AUTOLANDER_PORT is changed to fix the collision but this probe still hits the old 8080
advisory.suggested_fix: Set AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL default to http://localhost:${AUTOLANDER_PORT}/ (with AUTOLANDER_PORT a non-8080 value).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Constrain the autoheal Docker-socket access (e.g. socket-proxy limited to inspect+restart, or :ro where feasible) to reduce blast radius.
evidence: docker-compose.yml: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock (autoheal volumes)
Comment: "Needs the Docker socket (read-write) to inspect health + issue container restarts."
Docker socket RW == root-equivalent control of every container/image on the host
docker-compose.yml: image: willfarrell/autoheal (no tag or digest)
By contrast the gerrit service pins gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1 (compose-up.sh:18)
advisory.finding: The autoheal sidecar mounts the host Docker socket read-write (/var/run/docker.sock), granting the third-party willfarrell/autoheal container full Docker daemon control — effectively root on the host — which is a broad least-privilege/blast-radius grant for a container whose only job is restarting one labelled container.
merged_from: The autoheal sidecar image is pinned only to a floating tag (willfarrell/autoheal, i.e. :latest), so builds/deploys are non-reproducible and subject to silent upstream drift — especially concerning given this container holds the Docker socket.
scenarios: A compromise or malicious update of the willfarrell/autoheal image gains full control of the Docker daemon (all containers incl. gerrit) and the host

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the commit messages and smoke-check text with project.config so they reference only the `rebase` grant that is actually written (or add the grant if the platform truly requires it).
evidence: project.config:68-69: "there is no separate `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` ref permission; that form is silently ignored"
project.config:75-76: only `rebase = group Contributors` / `rebase = group Administrators` are written
setup-project.sh:148: commit msg "rebase/rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant"
smoke-check-autolander.sh 403 branch: "bot lacks rebase / rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader on refs/heads/*"
advisory.finding: Config vs. documentation drift on the rebase grant: project.config adds only `rebase = group ...` and its own comment states there is no separate `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` ref permission (it is 'silently ignored'), yet the commit subject, setup-project.sh commit message, and smoke-check-autolander.sh all describe granting BOTH `rebase` AND `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader`, and the smoke-check 403 failure message blames a missing rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant that is never written.
scenarios: An operator debugging a 403 chases a rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant that the declarative config never creates and cannot create
